about.title: Personal Injury Help in Delano, California
about.longDescription: Delano sees its share of everyday traffic trouble. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 139 injury collisions, with 196 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Corridors like Cecil Avenue, Garces Highway, High Street, and County Line Road carry a lot of that volume, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to be when reports cluster. If you or someone close to you was hurt in one of these incidents, or in a fall, workplace accident, or other mishap, sorting out next steps while healing can feel overwhelming. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Delano with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and we don't charge you anything. The attorneys in our network handle cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Our goal is simply to make it easier for you to get a knowledgeable professional looking at your situation without adding financial pressure while you're already dealing with enough.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for You

items.title: You Generally Have Two Years
items.desc: California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. That window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved, so it helps to move sooner rather than later.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit how much you can recover for non-economic harm like pain, suffering, or emotional distress.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost and no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Delano?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. If a government agency was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your timeline early.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Delano?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors like Cecil Avenue, Garces Highway, High Street, and County Line Road, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing more reports. These are neutral counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney — we are not a law firm and don't charge fees. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover money.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This is different from some other states, so it's worth discussing your specific situation with an attorney.
